title: Reserve Shield: Orchestrated Headroom & Tenant-Safe Burst PRD
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: A product requirements document describing Reserve Shield: a combined orchestration layer and control primitives for reserved pools that provide predictable headroom, safe tenant bursting, and automatic graceful fallback when capacity strain occurs.
background: Customers on Dedicated want predictable throughput for reserved pools while still being able to absorb transient spikes. Existing approaches either over-commit headroom (wasting capacity) or treat bursts as hard preemption events that risk noisy neighbor incidents. We need an orchestrated mechanism that provides configurable headroom guarantees, a safe burst borrowing protocol, and clear isolation/eviction controls that preserve SLOs and tenant SLAs.
user_stories: As a platform admin I want to configure per-tenant headroom policy so tenants can safely handle short spikes without manual intervention.
As an SRE I want automated burst arbitration that prefers non-preemptive mitigations (prefix caching, routing to compatible model variants) before evicting reserved workloads.
As a tenant owner I want visibility into my burst consumption and credits so I can predict bill/behavior and understand fallbacks.
As a product manager I want a clear rollback plan and canary for Reserve Shield to reduce blast radius on rollout.
goals: Provide configurable per-reservation headroom (0-25% of pool) that can be allocated as instantaneous burst capacity.
Implement a credit-based burst borrowing model with decay and replenishment rules to limit sustained overuse.
Build orchestration rules that attempt non-preemptive mitigations before soft-eviction and provide transparent fallback to hosted-compatible model variants.
Expose telemetry and tenant-facing dashboards showing reserved capacity, current headroom usage, credit ledger, and projected exhaustion time.
Support operator controls for emergency reclaim, manual preemption, and audit logs for all reclamation actions.
non_goals: This PRD does not cover multi-cloud placement optimizations or cross-region failover routing.
We will not change token-level billing models as part of this launch (billing integration tracked separately).
This work does not replace Dedicated autoscaler; autoscaling of pool size is out-of-scope for MVP.
requirements: R1: Headroom policy object available per reservation with parameters: headroom_pct (integer), credit_rate (tokens/min), max_burst_duration_minutes (integer), decay_window_minutes (integer).
R2: Credit ledger service that tracks per-reservation credits, issuance, usage, decay, and exposes read APIs for console and telemetry.

R3: Burst arbitration flow: try (a) KV/prefix cache reuse, (b) routing to same-architecture lower-cost variant, (c) short-latency queueing with SLA hints, (d) soft-eviction of opportunistic tasks. Each step is logged with reasoning.
R4: Soft-eviction must release KV caches and persist state to enable fast resume; operators must be able to identify evicted tenants and reason about impact.
R5: Tenant-facing dashboard surface: current_credits, credit_history, projected_exhaustion_iso_time, recent_burst_events (last 90 days).
R6: Operator controls: emergency_reclaim API (idempotent), manual_credit_adjust, and soft-eviction_exempt flag for safety-critical tenants.
R7: Audit logs for headroom allocations, credit consumption, arbitration decisions, and operator manual actions; retention configurable via console.
R8: Canary rollout plan with traffic-shaping for 1% -> 10% -> 50% of traffic and automatic rollback on defined SLO regressions.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Headroom policy object can be created/updated via API and reflected in console within 30s.
AC2: Credit ledger correctly issues and decays credits according to policy; simulated burst test shows credit depletion matches expected math within 5%.
AC3: Arbitration flow executed in policy-specified order; logs include decision reasons and latency impact for 100% of burst events during test window.
AC4: Soft-eviction sequences complete within target 45s and do not leak KV cache entries; integration test validates resume within 60s after capacity returns.
AC5: Dashboard surfaces all required fields and matches ledger reads; stakeholders can query last 90 days of events in under 5s.
AC6: Canary rollout shows no more than 10% increase in p99 latency for dedicated pool SLAs at 10% rollout and automatic rollback at 25% degradation threshold.
AC7: Operator emergency_reclaim API logs action and can reclaim up to 100% of headroom from a selected reservation; reclaim event creates an audit entry.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal alpha (engineers+SRE) with feature flag enabled on a subset of test clusters. Phase 1: Canary to 1% of production reserved pools with read-only dashboards. Phase 2: Expand to 10% with write path enabled for selected tenants. Phase 3: Gradual expansion to all dedicated pools pending metrics. Each phase gated by defined SLO metrics and a 48-hour monitoring window. Rollback is automatic on breach or via operator UI.
metrics: M3: Credit_exhaustion_rate (reservations per day that fully deplete credits)
telemetry: Emit event: reserve_shield.burst_attempt with fields (reservation_id, tenant_id, timestamp, pre_burst_credits, post_burst_credits, decision_path)
Emit event: reserve_shield.soft_eviction with fields (reservation_id, affected_tasks, duration_seconds, operator_action)
Expose graph: headroom consumption heatmap by cluster over last 30 days
privacy_compliance: No user PII is stored. Audit logs contain tenant IDs and operators; access to audit logs is RBAC-protected. Ensure KMS keys used for log storage meet Private deployment requirements.
dependencies: DEP-ENG-serve-runtime: KV cache eviction hooks and fast resume APIs must be implemented (ENG-2267)
DEP-OBS: Console telemetry panels and event ingestion schema updates (OBS-1422)
DEP-SCHED: Routing fallback capability to compatible variants (SCHED-3011)
Billing integration for credit metering (BILL-990) - tracked as separate workstream
open_questions: Q1: What is the default headroom_pct for new reservations? (suggestion: 10%)
Q2: Should credits be transferable between reservations within the same org? (security + accounting implications)
Q3: What SLAs do we promise for soft-evicted tasks vs hard-evicted tasks?
Q4: How should we surface projected cost impact to tenants when they consume burst credits?
risks: Risk of increased complexity in autoscale interactions causing oscillations; mitigate with conservative default policies and circuit breakers. Operational risk: operators may accidentally reclaim headroom from critical tenants — mitigate via prevent-default exemptions and two-step confirm flows. Monitoring gaps could mask slow credit leaks; include audits and simulated burst drills in SRE runbooks.
operational_playbook: Create SRE runbook: identify burst storms, how to trigger emergency_reclaim, how to interpret ledger and rollback Reserve Shield. Include checklist for canary expansion and rollback steps. Schedule weekly drills during Phase 1.
notes: Prototype used a simulated credit model with 100 tenants and showed 35% reduction in hard-evictions at equivalent capacity. We will refine decay math based on production telemetry. Keep billing and legal informed about any chargeable credit behaviors.
